annotation_description: Fetching a basic Island instead of Tundra is suboptimal here. With Swords to Plowshares in hand, having access to white mana is valuable. Tundra provides both blue and white mana, enabling Daze (as a blue source that can be returned) AND Swords to Plowshares. A basic Island only provides blue. Additionally, with two Wastelands in hand, the player has strong mana denial tools - having their own mana on a dual land that covers both colors is more resilient to their own mana constraints. The downside of Tundra (vulnerability to opponent's Wasteland) is real but relatively minor compared to the upside of having white mana access, especially since they have two Wastelands of their own and can fetch basics later.

annotation_description: Using Force of Will to counter a Daze on a Thundertrap Trainer (a 1/2 creature) is a significant overcommitment of resources. Force of Will costs a card from hand plus 1 life, making it a 2-for-1 against yourself. The Thundertrap Trainer is a low-impact creature - just a 1/2 that cantrips. The opponent only spent a free Daze (returning an Island) to counter it, meaning they invested very little. MiMo Stoic could have simply let the Daze resolve and lost only the Trainer, then replayed it next turn or deployed other threats. Instead, they're down Force of Will plus an exiled blue card (likely Brainstorm or Stern Scolding) to resolve a 1/2 creature. This leaves them without their best counterspell for the rest of the game against whatever threats the opponent presents.

annotation_description: Over-committed to counter a Thundertrap Trainer (a 1/2 value creature) by using Force of Will and exiling Brainstorm - one of the best cards in Legacy - to protect a Daze. After this exchange, hand is left with Scalding Tarn, 2x Wasteland, Swords to Plowshares, Island - extremely land-heavy with only one spell. Swords to Plowshares could cleanly answer the Trainer if it resolved, and Brainstorm was critical to dig out of a land-heavy hand.

With the opponent at only 2 Islands and tapped out after spending Force of Will, this was a prime opportunity for mana denial. Playing Wasteland to destroy one of their Islands would leave them at 1 land with depleted resources, and with a second Wasteland in hand, could potentially lock them out entirely next turn.

Playing Scalding Tarn instead of Wasteland misses an opportunity for immediate mana denial against an opponent with only two Islands. Destroying one of their Islands with Wasteland would cut them to one land, creating a massive tempo advantage while the opponent is already down resources (Force of Will and Thundertrap Trainer in graveyard).

annotation_description: Force of Will's flashback cost is {3}{U}{U}, which is extremely difficult to pay with only 2 lands on board. The alternate cost (1 life + exile blue card) cannot be used as a substitute for flashback costs. Stern Scolding's flashback cost of {U} would be immediately available and relevant in Legacy where many key creatures have power/toughness 2 or less.

Cast Ponder before playing a land. Should play Wasteland first (free land drop), potentially using it to destroy one of the opponent's tapped Islands to cut them to 1 land, then cast Ponder with the Island. Playing land before casting spells is fundamental sequencing - it preserves options and provides more information before committing mana.

When ordering cards from Ponder, the player put Misty Rainforest on the bottom and Stifle on top. Given their hand of 2x Wasteland and 2x Swords to Plowshares with only 2 lands on board, they desperately need a land drop. Misty Rainforest is a fetchland that would both provide an immediate land drop AND thin the deck. Stifle is a narrow reactive card that doesn't address their current needs - they're behind on board with a Snapcaster Mage threatening them, and they need to develop their mana base to cast their Swords to Plowshares effectively while also deploying Wastelands.

Playing Wasteland without immediately using it to destroy one of the opponent's Islands is debatable. The opponent has only 2 Islands (both tapped) and a Snapcaster Mage. Destroying an Island now (or threatening to next turn) could be strong since the opponent is mana-light. However, the bigger question is whether to cast Swords to Plowshares on Snapcaster Mage first (while opponent's lands are tapped) before playing the land. With Tundra untapped and opponent tapped out, this was a window to remove Snapcaster Mage for free without worrying about countermagic. Playing the Wasteland first is fine sequencing-wise since it doesn't use mana, but not casting Swords on the Snapcaster while the opponent is tapped out could be a missed opportunity - though keeping Swords for bigger threats like a future Murktide from the opponent is also reasonable.

Sonnet Vorthos passed the turn without taking any action despite having productive options available. The opponent has a Snapcaster Mage (2/1) on board and only two tapped Islands. Sonnet Vorthos could have cast Swords to Plowshares on the Snapcaster Mage (using Tundra for W) to remove the threat and deny future flashback value, or activated Wasteland to destroy one of the opponent's Islands (leaving them with just one land). Both of these lines generate meaningful advantage. Additionally, Phelia is listed in the graveyard so there's nothing to attack with, but passing without using Swords or Wasteland when the opponent is tapped out wastes a clean window to act.

Sonnet Vorthos has an untapped Wasteland and the opponent has no nonbasic lands (only two basic Islands), so Wasteland activation wouldn't help there. However, the player missed the opportunity to cast Swords to Plowshares on the opponent's Snapcaster Mage. Snapcaster Mage is a 2/1 that can attack and has already provided its ETB value, but removing it prevents 2 damage per turn and denies a potential blocker. More importantly, with the opponent having only 2 Islands tapped, this is a window where they can't counter the Swords (no mana available). Leaving the Snapcaster alive while having two Swords and an untapped Tundra is a missed opportunity to use a removal spell when the opponent is tapped out.

Sonnet Vorthos has Snapcaster Mage on the opponent's board and Swords to Plowshares in hand with Tundra untapped to cast it. The Snapcaster Mage is a threat that can attack and has already provided value (giving flashback to a spell in graveyard). More importantly, Sonnet Vorthos could use Wasteland to destroy one of the opponent's Islands, constraining their mana. With the opponent at only 2 Islands, destroying one would significantly limit their ability to cast spells. Swords to Plowshares on Snapcaster before combat prevents 2 damage and removes a body. While passing isn't terrible, using Wasteland on an Island here is free value that constrains the opponent's mana development.

message: Select an Island or Mountain card
annotation_description: Fetched Volcanic Island into an opponent's untapped Wasteland when a basic Mountain would have provided the same mana for Flame of Anor ({1}{U}{R}) without being vulnerable to Wasteland destruction. With 2 Islands already in play, a basic Mountain gives the exact same casting capability.

Casting Flame of Anor in precombat main phase before attacking with Snapcaster Mage. The opponent has no creatures to block, so Snapcaster should attack first. Flame of Anor is an instant and could be cast in post-combat main or even on opponent's end step. Casting it precombat taps out MiMo before dealing 2 combat damage, and if the drawn cards include something useful to play, having already tapped out limits options.
Chose Sonnet Vorthos as the target for Flame of Anor's 'draw two cards' mode, giving the opponent two free cards instead of drawing them yourself. This is a ~4-card swing in card advantage.

MiMo Stoic chose to have the opponent (Sonnet Vorthos) draw two cards from Flame of Anor instead of themselves. This gives the opponent a massive card advantage for absolutely no benefit. MiMo Stoic had only 2 cards in hand (one being the Flame of Anor on the stack) and desperately needed cards.

Sonnet Vorthos declined to cast Swords to Plowshares on Snapcaster Mage before it attacked, taking 2 damage. While they could cast it after attackers are declared (and still can during the declare blockers step or after damage), the decision to pass priority here without using Swords is not necessarily wrong since they can still respond. However, with Snapcaster Mage having already provided its ETB value (giving Stern Scolding flashback), removing it is reasonable. The real question is whether using Swords on a 2/1 is worth the card when Sonnet Vorthos is at 17 life. Taking 2 damage to save a Swords for a bigger threat is defensible, but Snapcaster is a key creature in the opponent's deck and they have no other board presence. Using Wasteland on Volcanic Island during their combat to deny them red mana could also be considered.

Sonnet Vorthos declined to cast Swords to Plowshares on the attacking Snapcaster Mage (which is tapped, indicating it attacked). Snapcaster Mage is a 2/1 that already provided its ETB value (likely flashing back Stern Scolding or similar), and removing it now costs only W mana (Tundra is untapped) while preventing future damage. More importantly, removing Snapcaster Mage puts another instant in the graveyard, which helps fuel Murktide Regent's delve. With 6 cards already in graveyard, removing Snapcaster now and having 7 cards in graveyard (plus lands potentially) makes casting Murktide much easier. The opponent also has Volcanic Island meaning they have red mana for potential burn/removal, so racing is important.

Sonnet Vorthos declined to use Wasteland to destroy opponent's Volcanic Island (their only red source) or cast Swords to Plowshares on the tapped Snapcaster Mage. The Snapcaster Mage is a meaningful threat that already provided value (likely flashing back Stern Scolding to counter Phelia based on the graveyard state). More importantly, Swords to Plowshares should be cast on the Snapcaster Mage while it's tapped and the opponent has no untapped mana to protect it - waiting gives the opponent a chance to untap and hold up countermagic. Wasteland on Volcanic Island would also cut off the opponent's red mana, potentially stranding cards in hand.

Sonnet Vorthos cast Murktide Regent before playing a land (Misty Rainforest or Wasteland were available). While Murktide can be cast via Delve using the 6 cards in graveyard (Flooded Strand, Force of Will, Daze, Scalding Tarn, Phelia, Ponder) plus 1 blue mana, playing Misty Rainforest first and cracking it would put another card in the graveyard, potentially allowing Murktide to enter with more +1/+1 counters (one more instant/sorcery exiled). Additionally, casting Murktide before land drop means if it gets countered, they've missed the opportunity to have an extra land in play. Also, casting the creature in precombat main phase rather than waiting gives the opponent more information. However, the bigger issue is sequencing: Wasteland could have been used to destroy the opponent's Volcanic Island before they untap, cutting them off red mana sources, but that should probably happen before committing Murktide into potential countermagic. Playing Misty Rainforest first, fetching an Island, would add a fetchland to graveyard for Delve fuel and provide an additional mana source as backup.

Sonnet Vorthos passed priority in precombat main without taking any action, despite having a strong line available. The reasoning mentions 'Misty Rainforest activation is on the stack' but the stack is empty, suggesting confused reasoning. They could play Wasteland from hand, sacrifice the existing Wasteland to destroy Volcanic Island (cutting opponent off red mana), and cast Murktide Regent for UU as a large flyer while Snapcaster Mage is tapped.

MiMo Stoic declined to cast Flame of Anor despite having exactly the mana ({1}{U}{R} from two Islands and Volcanic Island) and a Wizard (Snapcaster Mage) on the battlefield. Drawing two cards would significantly improve their position. They have a second copy of Flame of Anor for future removal needs, and the opponent's Wasteland threatens to destroy Volcanic Island, potentially stranding both copies.

Passed the turn without using Wasteland to destroy opponent's Volcanic Island (their only red source) or casting Swords to Plowshares on the tapped Snapcaster Mage. Destroying Volcanic Island would cut the opponent off red mana, limiting their options significantly. Removing Snapcaster while tapped prevents it from being used to flash back spells.

MiMo Stoic targeted the opponent with Flame of Anor's 'draw two cards' mode, giving the opponent two free cards instead of drawing them themselves. This is a ~4-card swing in card advantage — MiMo Stoic had only 1 card left in hand and desperately needed resources.

Failed to activate Wasteland to destroy opponent's Volcanic Island before casting Murktide Regent in main phase 2. Destroying Volcanic Island would cut the opponent off red mana, preventing potential Flame of Anor (which deals 5 damage to a creature and could kill Murktide). Sonnet Vorthos has enough mana to cast Murktide with Delve using just Island + two Tundras.

Casting Flame of Anor now only gets the 'draw 2 cards' mode since the opponent has no creatures or artifacts. With Snapcaster Mage as a Wizard, Flame of Anor could choose TWO modes - but the second useful mode (deal 5 to a creature or destroy an artifact) has no valid target. Holding it for when the opponent deploys a creature would allow a 2-for-1 (draw 2 + kill a creature), which is significantly more value.

MiMo Stoic targeted the opponent with Flame of Anor's 'draw two cards' mode, giving the opponent two free cards instead of drawing them themselves. There is no strategic reason to let the opponent draw two cards in this situation.

MiMo Stoic has Snapcaster Mage (a Wizard) on the battlefield, enabling Flame of Anor to choose two modes. With no opponent creatures or artifacts, the relevant mode is 'draw two cards.' They have exactly the mana to cast it ({1}{U}{R} from Island, Island, Volcanic Island) while leaving Plains untapped for Swords to Plowshares as protection on the opponent's turn. Passing on drawing two cards for free is a significant value loss.

Cast Murktide Regent before playing a land for the turn. Playing Wasteland (as land drop) or Flooded Strand first would provide an extra mana source, requiring one fewer card to delve (preserving graveyard resources). Additionally, using the existing Wasteland to destroy opponent's Volcanic Island before casting Murktide would cut their blue mana and reduce the chance of a counterspell resolving.

Player passed priority in precombat main without playing a land or taking any action, seemingly confused about the game state (reasoning claims 'Murktide is on the stack' when it's still in hand). They missed the opportunity to play Flooded Strand, crack it for a land, and potentially cast Murktide Regent this turn as a large threat (with 9 cards in graveyard, delving 5 makes it cost just UU and enter as an 8/8 flyer). They also could have activated Wasteland to destroy opponent's Volcanic Island.

Playing Wasteland as a land instead of Flooded Strand is suboptimal. The second Wasteland only produces colorless mana, while Flooded Strand can be cracked to fetch a blue source, thin the deck, and add a card to the graveyard to fuel Murktide Regent's Delve. They already have one Wasteland in play to threaten the opponent's Volcanic Island.

Sonnet Vorthos passed the turn without using Wasteland to destroy one of MiMo Stoic's nonbasic lands (Volcanic Island). With 4 lands on board including 2 Tundras and an Island, they have adequate mana. Destroying Volcanic Island would cut off MiMo Stoic's red mana source, potentially preventing cards like Flame of Anor. The player seemed confused about why Murktide Regent wasn't castable and passed without taking any action, missing the opportunity to use Wasteland proactively.

Cast Flame of Anor before playing Prismatic Vista as a land drop. Should play and potentially crack Prismatic Vista first to have additional mana available after drawing two cards from Flame of Anor, and to get a basic land safe from the opponent's two Wastelands.

Should activate Prismatic Vista before casting Flame of Anor to thin the deck before drawing 2 cards and to fetch a basic land for better Wasteland protection. The opponent has two Wastelands threatening the nonbasic lands.
Flame of Anor's draw two cards mode was targeted at the opponent instead of themselves. This gives the opponent a free 2-for-0 card advantage for no reason whatsoever.

With Flame of Anor on the stack (likely choosing the draw 2 mode since there's no Wizard and no artifact/creature target worth hitting), MiMo Stoic should activate Prismatic Vista in response to thin the deck before the draw resolves. Additionally, fetching a basic land would protect against the opponent's two Wastelands.

MiMo Stoic targeted the opponent with Flame of Anor's 'draw two cards' mode, giving the opponent two free cards instead of drawing them for themselves. With no enemy creatures or artifacts to target, drawing two cards for yourself was the only beneficial mode available.

Sonnet Vorthos has two Wastelands and the opponent has Volcanic Island and Prismatic Vista as nonbasic lands. Using Wasteland to destroy Volcanic Island would cut off the opponent's only red source, potentially stranding cards like Flame of Anor. However, the opponent has 3 Islands plus Plains, so they still have plenty of mana. The decision to hold Wastelands is defensible since preserving mana sources matters when at 14 life and needing to cast Murktide Regent, but destroying the Volcanic Island to cut off red could have been valuable.

Sonnet Vorthos has two Wastelands and the opponent has Volcanic Island and Prismatic Vista as nonbasic lands. Activating Wasteland to destroy Volcanic Island during MiMo's postcombat main (after they've presumably tapped out or used their mana) would deny them their only red source and constrain their mana. With Murktide Regent in hand needing to be cast soon, keeping tempo pressure on the opponent's mana is important. However, Sonnet Vorthos also needs lands to cast Murktide Regent (which costs 7 minus delve), so sacrificing a Wasteland reduces their own mana. With 9 cards in graveyard, Murktide could potentially be cast for UU with enough delve fuel, so losing a land to Wasteland might be acceptable. The decision is debatable but passing up the opportunity to cut off the opponent's red mana (their only Volcanic Island) when you have two Wastelands available is worth questioning.

Murktide Regent is on the stack and Sonnet Vorthos has Force of Will in hand (with no blue cards to exile for alternative cost, but could hard-cast it with 5 mana available: Island, Tundra, Tundra, Wasteland, Wasteland = only 4 colored mana sources plus Wastelands for colorless = UUWCC which isn't enough for 3UU). Actually, looking more carefully: Island (U), Tundra (U/W), Tundra (U/W), Wasteland (C), Wasteland (C) = at best UUUCC or UUWCC, which doesn't cast Force of Will (3UU needs 5 mana with 2 blue). They have UUWCC = 5 mana but only 2-3 blue. Force of Will costs 3UU = they need UU + 3 generic = UU + UWC or UU + WCC. With Island+Tundra for UU and Tundra+Wasteland+Wasteland for WCC = yes, they CAN hard-cast Force of Will for 3UU! Murktide Regent is a massive flying threat (likely 8/8+ with delve exiling instants/sorceries from graveyard). Instead of countering it with Force of Will, they played Flooded Strand, allowing Murktide to resolve. This is a game-losing mistake - Murktide Regent with multiple +1/+1 counters is extremely difficult to deal with, especially when the opponent has counter backup.

Sonnet Vorthos declined to use Wasteland to destroy one of MiMo Stoic's nonbasic lands (Volcanic Island or Prismatic Vista). MiMo Stoic has Volcanic Island as their only red source, and destroying it would cut them off red mana entirely, potentially preventing Flame of Anor or other red spells. However, Sonnet Vorthos may be holding Wastelands to use at a more impactful moment, and they need lands to cast Murktide Regent. The opponent has 5 lands including only one nonbasic worth targeting (Volcanic Island), so using Wasteland on Volcanic Island to deny red mana seems reasonable, especially since Sonnet Vorthos has 6 lands and Murktide can be cast cheaply with Delve (9 cards in graveyard means it could cost as little as UU).

Opponent has two Wastelands on the battlefield threatening to destroy Prismatic Vista for free card disadvantage. Cracking Prismatic Vista now to get a Wasteland-proof basic land is virtually free and protects against a clear on-board threat.

MiMo Stoic passed with Flame of Anor available that could draw 2 cards (the only useful mode with no creatures or artifacts on board). The opponent has 2 Wastelands that threaten Volcanic Island, which is MiMo's only red source. If Volcanic Island gets destroyed, Flame of Anor becomes uncastable. Drawing 2 cards in this board stall would provide significant card advantage.

Sonnet Vorthos has two Wastelands and the opponent has Volcanic Island and Prismatic Vista as nonbasic lands. Using Wasteland to destroy Volcanic Island would cut the opponent off red mana (relevant for Flame of Anor and other red spells) and reduce their mana development. With 6 lands in play and only needing to cast Murktide Regent (which uses Delve) and holding Force of Will plus Swords to Plowshares, sacrificing a Wasteland would still leave adequate mana. Declining to use Wasteland when there's no downside to mana-denying the opponent is a missed opportunity.

Sonnet Vorthos declined to activate either Wasteland to destroy one of MiMo Stoic's nonbasic lands (Volcanic Island or Prismatic Vista). With the opponent at 5 lands including two nonbasics, destroying Volcanic Island would cut off their red mana source entirely, which is relevant for cards like Flame of Anor. Wasteland is a tempo tool that should be used proactively, especially when the player is behind on life (13 vs 20) and struggling to resolve threats. The player appeared to be frustrated with not being able to cast Murktide Regent and passed without using available resources.

Cast Flame of Anor during own main phase instead of activating Prismatic Vista first to thin the deck before drawing 2 cards. Additionally, as an instant, Flame of Anor could be cast at end of opponent's turn to preserve information and flexibility. The main concrete mistake is not fetching first before drawing.

MiMo Stoic chose Sonnet Vorthos as the target for Flame of Anor's 'draw two cards' mode, giving the opponent two free cards instead of drawing them themselves. With no creatures or artifacts on the battlefield, the draw mode was the only useful option, and it should have targeted themselves.
